translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era the Liao chieftain Li Fozi of Jiaozhou rebelled and held the old Yue capital. Yang Su said Fang had a commander's mind; he was made campaign commander of the Jiaozhou route at the head of twenty-seven camps. His discipline was severe but he loved his men. Chief clerk Jing Deliang fell mortally ill at Yinzhou and had to be left behind; Fang wept at parting so that passersby were moved—many called him a true general. At Dujiang Ridge he sent Song Zuan, He Gui, Yan Yuan, and others to break the enemy, then advanced on Fozi, warned him of ruin, and took his surrender to the capital. The stubborn who might rise again were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，有馮昱、王纲、楊武通、陳永貴、房兆，俱為邊將，名顯當時．

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era there were Feng Yu, Wang Gang, Yang Wutong, Chen Yonggui, and Fang Zhao, all frontier generals whose names were illustrious in their time.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era Feng Yu, Wang Gang, Yang Wutong, Chen Yonggui, and Fang Zhao were frontier commanders whose names stood out in their day.

sentences.zh: 馮昱、王纲

translations.literal: Feng Yu and Wang Gang
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yu and Wang Gang

sentences.zh: 昱、纲並不知何許人．昱多權略，有武藝．文帝初為丞相，以行軍總管與王誼、李威等討平叛蠻，拜柱國．開皇初，又以行軍總管屯乙弗泊備胡，每戰常大剋捷．纲驍勇善射，每以行軍總管屯兵江北以禦陳，為陳人所憚．伐陳之役，及高智慧反，攻討皆有殊績．位柱國、白水郡公．

translations.literal: Yu and Gang—neither is known from what place. Yu had many stratagems and martial arts. When the Emperor first became Chancellor, as campaign commander with Wang Yi, Li Wei, and others he pacified rebellious barbarians and was appointed Pillar of State. In the beginning of Kaihuang he again as campaign commander garrisoned Yifu Marsh to guard against the Hu; in every battle he often won great victories. Gang was fierce and brave and skilled in shooting; each time as campaign commander he garrisoned troops north of the Yangtze to guard against Chen and was feared by the Chen people. In the campaign against Chen and when Gao Zhihui rebelled, in attack and suppression he all had outstanding merit. He held the rank of Pillar of State and Duke of Baishui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Yu nor Gang's origin is recorded. Yu was full of stratagems and skilled in arms. When Wen first became regent he campaigned with Wang Yi and Li Wei against rebel tribes and was made a pillar of state. Early in Kaihuang he garrisoned Yifu Marsh against the Hu and won repeated great victories. Gang was fierce, a fine archer, long stationed north of the Yangtze against Chen and feared by the Chen. In the conquest of Chen and Gao Zhihui's rebellion he won outstanding merit and became pillar of state and duke of Baishui commandery.

sentences.zh: 楊武通

translations.literal: Yang Wutong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wutong

sentences.zh: 武通，弘農華陰人，性果烈，善馳射．數以行軍總管討西南夷，以功封白水郡公，拜左武纫將軍．時党項羌屢為邊患，朝廷以其有威名，使鎮邊，歷岷、蘭二州總管．復與周法尚討嘉州叛獠，法尚軍初不利，武通為賊斷歸路．於是束馬懸車，出賊不意，頻戰破之．賊知其孤軍無援，傾部落而至．武通轉岗數百里，為賊所拒，四面路絕．武通輕騎挑戰，墜馬，為賊所執，殺而噉之．

translations.literal: Wutong was a man of Huayin in Hongnong, fierce and resolute in nature, skilled in mounted archery. Several times as campaign commander he attacked the southwestern barbarians; through merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Baishui Commandery and appointed General of the Left Martial Guard. At that time the Qiang of Dangzhou repeatedly were a border trouble; the court, because he had a famous reputation, sent him to guard the frontier; he successively served as Commander-in-Chief of Min and Lan Prefectures. Again with Zhou Fashang he attacked the rebel Liao of Jiazhou; Fashang's army at first was unfavorable; Wutong had his return road cut by the bandits. Thereupon he bound horses and hung carts, came out where the bandits did not expect, and repeatedly fought and broke them. The bandits knew his lone army had no support; the whole tribe came down upon him. Wutong fought in turn for several hundred li, was blocked by the bandits on four sides, and the roads were cut off. Wutong with light horse challenged battle, fell from his horse, was seized by the bandits, killed and eaten.
translations.idiomatic: Wutong came from Huayin in Hongnong—fierce, a master of mounted archery. Repeated campaigns in the southwest won him the dukedom of Baishui and the left martial guard. When Dangzhou Qiang troubled the border, his name alone sent him to Min and Lan as commander-in-chief. With Zhou Fashang he fought rebel Liao in Jiazhou; Fashang faltered and the rebels cut Wutong's retreat. He bound wheels, lowered carts over cliffs, struck where they did not expect, and broke them again and again. Seeing him isolated, the tribes massed. For hundreds of li he fought on every side until the roads were gone. He challenged on a light horse, fell, was taken, killed, and eaten.

sentences.zh: 陳永貴

translations.literal: Chen Yonggui
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yonggui

sentences.zh: 永貴，隴右胡人，本姓白，以勇烈，為文帝所親愛．數以行軍總管領邊，[一０]每戰必單騎陷陣．位柱國、蘭利二州總管，封北陳郡公．

translations.literal: Yonggui was a Hu man of Longyou, originally surnamed Bai; because of his fierce valor he was loved by the Emperor. Several times as campaign commander he led the frontier, [10] and in every battle he always charged alone into the array. He held the rank of Pillar of State, Commander-in-Chief of Lan and Li Prefectures, and Duke of Beichen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggui was a Longyou Hu, family name Bai; his fierce courage won the emperor's favor. As frontier campaign commander [10] he always charged the line alone. He became pillar of state, commander-in-chief of Lan and Li, and duke of Beichen commandery.

sentences.zh: 兆，代人，本姓屋引氏，剛毅有武略．頻為行軍總管攻胡，以功位至柱國、徐州總管．並史失其事．

translations.literal: Zhao was a man of Dai, originally surnamed Wuyin; firm and resolute with military strategy. Repeatedly as campaign commander he attacked the Hu; through merit he reached Pillar of State and Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou. The histories have all lost their accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhao came from Dai, originally of the Wuyin clan—hard, martial, repeatedly sent against the Hu until he was pillar of state and commander-in-chief of Xuzhou. The histories no longer record their deeds.

sentences.zh: 杜彥，雲中人也．父遷，葛榮之亂，徙家于豳．

translations.literal: Du Yan was a native of Yunzhong. His father Qian, in Ge Rong's disorder, moved his family to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan came from Yunzhong. His father Qian, in the disorders of Ge Rong, had moved the family to Bin.

sentences.zh: 彥性勇決，善騎射．仕周，以軍功累遷隴州刺史，賜爵永安縣伯．隋文帝為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉遲迥，以功進位上開府，改封襄武縣侯，拜魏郡太守．開皇初，授丹州刺史，進爵為公．徵為左武纫將軍．平陳之役，以行軍總管與韓擒相繼而進．及陳平，賜物五千段，粟六千石，進位柱國，賜子寶安爵昌陽縣公．高智慧等之作亂，復以行軍總管從楊素討平之，斬其渠帥．賊李鲶擁红據彭山，彥襲擊破之，斬鲶，傳其首．又擊徐州、宜封二洞，悉平．賜奴婢百餘口．拜洪州總管，有能名．

translations.literal: Yan was brave and decisive in nature, skilled in riding and shooting. In Zhou, through military merit he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Longzhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Yong'an County. When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuchi Jiong; through merit he was promoted to Upper Opening Grandee, changed to Marquis of Xiangwu County, and appointed Administrator of Wei Commandery. In the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Danzhou and advanced in rank to Duke. He was summoned as General of the Left Martial Guard. In the Chen campaign, as campaign commander he advanced in succession with Han Qin. When Chen was pacified he was given five thousand lengths of goods, six thousand piculs of grain, promoted to Pillar of State, and his son Bao'an was enfeoffed as Duke of Changyang County. When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled, again as campaign commander he followed Yang Su to pacify them and beheaded their chieftains. The bandit Li Nian held troops and occupied Pengshan; Yan made a surprise attack and broke them, beheaded Nian, and sent his head. He also attacked the caves of Xuzhou and Yifeng; all were pacified. He was given more than a hundred male and female slaves. He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Hongzhou and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was bold and decisive, expert with horse and bow. Under the Zhou he rose to governor of Longzhou and baron of Yong'an. As Wen's regent he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuchi Jiong, became upper opening grandee, marquis of Xiangwu, and prefect of Wei commandery. In early Kaihuang he was governor of Danzhou and then a duke, summoned as left martial guard general. In the Chen war he marched in tandem with Han Qin; after the fall of Chen he received five thousand rolls of goods and six thousand piculs of grain, was made pillar of state, and his son Bao'an was enfeoffed duke of Changyang. He campaigned under Yang Su against Gao Zhihui and beheaded rebel leaders; surprised Li Nian at Pengshan and sent up his head; pacified the Xuzhou and Yifeng cave peoples; was given more than a hundred slaves; and became commander-in-chief of Hongzhou with a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 及雲州總管賀婁子幹卒，上悼惜者久之，因謂侍臣曰：「榆林國之重鎮，安得子幹之輩乎？

translations.literal: When Commander-in-Chief of Yunzhou Helou Zigan died, the Emperor mourned and prized him for a long time, and therefore said to his attendants: "Yulin is a vital stronghold of the state—where can we find men like Zigan?
translations.idiomatic: When Helou Zigan, commander-in-chief of Yunzhou, died, the emperor mourned him long and asked his court: "Yulin is a pillar of the realm—where shall we find another like Zigan?

sentences.zh: 」後數日，上曰：「莫過杜彥．」於是徵拜雲州總管．北夷畏憚，胡馬不敢至塞．後朝廷追錄前功，賜子寶虔爵承縣公．十八年，遼東之役，以行軍總管從漢王至營州．上以彥曉習軍旅，令總統五十營事．及還，拜朔州總管．突厥寇雲州，上令楊素擊走之，猶恐為邊患，復拜彥雲州總管．以疾徵還，卒．

translations.literal: " Several days later the Emperor said: "None surpasses Du Yan." Thereupon he was summoned and appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yunzhou. The northern barbarians feared and respected him; Hu horses did not dare come to the passes. Later the court recorded former merit and his son Baoqian was enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng County. In the eighteenth year, on the Liaodong campaign, as campaign commander he followed the Prince of Han to Yingzhou. The Emperor, because Yan was skilled in military affairs, ordered him to command the affairs of fifty camps. When he returned he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou. The Turks raided Yunzhou; the Emperor ordered Yang Su to attack and drive them off, yet still feared border trouble and again appointed Yan Commander-in-Chief of Yunzhou. He was summoned back for illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later he said: "No one surpasses Du Yan," and Yan was made commander-in-chief of Yunzhou. The northern peoples feared him; Turk horses did not come to the passes. Later the court honored old service and his son Baoqian received the dukedom of Cheng. In year 18, on the Liaodong expedition, he followed the Prince of Han to Yingzhou; knowing his craft, the emperor set him over fifty camps. Returning, he was commander-in-chief of Shuozhou. When Turks raided Yunzhou, Yang Su drove them off, but fearing further harm the emperor gave Yan Yunzhou again. He was recalled ill and died.

sentences.zh: 杜寶虔

translations.literal: Du Baoqian
translations.idiomatic: Du Baoqian

sentences.zh: 子寶虔，大業末，至文城郡丞．

translations.literal: His son Baoqian, at the end of Daye, reached the post of Vice Administrator of Wencheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoqian, at the end of the Daye era, was vice administrator of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 周搖字世安，河南洛陽人也．其先與魏同源，初姓普乃，及居洛陽，改為周氏．曾祖拔拔，祖右六肱，俱為北平王．父恕延，歷行臺僕射、南荊州總管．

translations.literal: Zhou Yao, styled Shi'an, was a native of Luoyang in Henan. His ancestors shared the same origin as Wei; originally surnamed Punai, and when they dwelt in Luoyang they changed to the Zhou clan. His great-grandfather Bababa, his grandfather Youruliugan, and both were Princes of Beiping. His father Nuyan successively held the posts of Director of the Bureau of the Palace, Commander-in-Chief of Nanjing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yao, courtesy name Shi'an, came from Luoyang in Henan. His line shared Wei origins, first surnamed Punai; in Luoyang they took the name Zhou. His great-grandfather Bababa and grandfather Youruliugan had both been princes of Beiping; his father Nuyan had been director of the palace bureau and commander-in-chief of Nanjing province.

sentences.zh: 搖少剛毅，有武藝，性謹厚，動遵法度．仕魏，位開府儀同三司．周閔帝受禪，賜姓車非氏，封金水郡公．歷鳳、楚二州刺史，吏人安之．從平齊，以戰功超授柱國，進封夔國公．未幾，拜晉州總管．時隋文帝為定州總管，文獻皇后自京師赴州，路經搖所，主禮甚薄．既而白后曰：「公廨甚富於財，限法不敢輒費．又王臣無得刋私．」其質直如此．帝以其奉法，每嘉之．及為丞相，徙封濟北郡公，拜豫州總管．帝受禪，復姓周氏．

translations.literal: Yao in youth was firm and resolute, with martial arts; his nature was careful and thick, and in movement he followed law and measure. In Wei he held the rank of Opening Grandee, Yitong of the Third Rank. When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication he was given the surname Chefei and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinshui Commandery. He successively served as Governor of Feng and Chu Prefectures; officials and people were at peace under him. He followed in pacifying Qi; through military merit he was specially promoted to Pillar of State and advanced to Duke of the State of Kui. Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Jinzhou. At that time Emperor Wen of Sui was Commander-in-Chief of Dingzhou; the Empress Dowager Wen came from the capital to the province; passing Yao's place, the reception was very thin. He then told the Empress: "The public offices are very rich in wealth; the law does not permit casual expenditure. Moreover as the king's ministers one may not have private engravings." He was so upright and plain. The Emperor because he upheld the law always praised him. When he became Chancellor he was transferred to Duke of Jibei Commandery and appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yuzhou. When the Emperor received the abdication he restored the surname Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yao was stern and martial, careful and law-abiding. Under the Wei he was opening grandee, yitong of the third rank. When Emperor Min of Zhou took the throne he received the surname Chefei and the dukedom of Jinshui. He governed Feng and Chu peacefully, followed the Qi campaigns, and was raised to pillar of state and duke of Kui. Soon he was commander-in-chief of Jinzhou. When the future Emperor Wen was commander-in-chief of Dingzhou, Empress Wen came from the capital; passing Yao's post she was entertained very sparely. He told her: "The government stores are rich; the law forbids waste, and a king's minister may keep no private seal." The emperor prized his integrity. As regent Wen made him duke of Jibei and commander-in-chief of Yuzhou; at the accession the Zhou surname was restored.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，突厥寇邊，燕、薊多被其患，前總管李崇為虜所殺，上思所以鎮之，曰：「無以加周搖．」拜為幽州總管、六州五十鎮諸軍事．搖修障塞，謹斥候，邊人安之．徙壽、襄二州總管，俱有能名，進上柱國．以老乞骸骨，上勞之曰：「公歷仕三代，保茲遐壽，良足善也．」賜坐褥．歸第，終於家，諡曰恭．

translations.literal: In the beginning of Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; Yan and Ji were much afflicted by them; the former Commander-in-Chief Li Chong was killed by the barbarians; the Emperor thought how to hold the region and said: "There is none to surpass Zhou Yao." He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou and Military Affairs of Six Prefectures and Fifty Garrisons. Yao repaired barriers and passes and carefully set outposts; the frontier people were at peace. He was transferred as Commander-in-Chief of Shou and Xiang Prefectures; in both he had a name for ability and was advanced to Senior Pillar of State. He begged to retire on account of age; the Emperor comforted him: "You, sir, served three dynasties and preserved this long life—truly enough to be praised." He was given a seat cushion. Returning home he died at his residence; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang the Turks ravaged Yan and Ji; Commander-in-Chief Li Chong was killed; the emperor said, "Only Zhou Yao will do," and made him commander-in-chief of Youzhou over six prefectures and fifty garrisons. He repaired walls and watches; the frontier rested easy. He held Shou and Xiang with the same reputation and became senior pillar of state. He asked to retire; the emperor comforted him: "You have served three dynasties and kept a long life—well done." He was given a seat mat, went home, and died there with the posthumous name Gong ("respectful").

sentences.zh: 獨孤楷

translations.literal: Dugu Kai
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Kai

sentences.zh: 獨孤楷字脩則，不知何許人也，本姓李氏．父屯，從齊神武帝與周師戰于沙苑，齊師敗績，因為柱國獨孤信所禽，配為士伍，給使信家，漸得親近，因賜姓獨孤氏．

translations.literal: Dugu Kai, styled Xiuzi, is not known from what place; his original surname was Li. His father Tun, following Qi Emperor Shenwu in battle with the Zhou army at Shayuan, the Qi army was defeated, and he was captured by Pillar of State Dugu Xin and assigned as a common soldier to serve in Xin's household, gradually gaining closeness, and was therefore given the surname Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Kai, courtesy name Xiuzi, is of unknown origin; his family had been Li. His father Tun, fighting for Northern Qi's Emperor Shenwu against the Zhou at Shayuan, was captured when Qi fell, made a bondman in the household of the pillar Dugu Xin, won trust, and received the Dugu surname.

sentences.zh: 楷少謹厚，便弄馬槊，為宇文護執刀．數從征伐，賜爵廣阿縣公，拜右侍下大夫．從韋孝寬平淮南，以功賜子景雲爵西河縣公．隋文帝為丞相，進開府，領親信兵．及受禪，拜右監門將軍，進封汝陽郡公．

translations.literal: Kai in youth was careful and thick, skilled with horse and spear, and served as sword-bearer for Yuwen Hu. Several times he followed campaigns; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Guang'a County and appointed Right Attendant Lower Grandee. He followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan; through merit his son Jingyun was enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe County. When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor he was advanced to Opening Grandee and led the trusted troops. When he received the abdication he was appointed General of the Right Gate Guards and advanced to Duke of Ruyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kai in youth was steady and skilled with lance and saddle, and bore the sword for Yuwen Hu. Campaigns won him the dukedom of Guang'a and the post of right attendant lower grandee. He followed Wei Xiaokuan in Huainan; his son Jingyun received Xihe county. When Wen was regent he became opening grandee commanding the trusted guard; at the accession he was right gate-guard general and duke of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，出為原州總管．時蜀王秀鎮益州，上征之，猶豫未發．朝廷恐秀生變，拜楷益州總管，馳傳代之．秀果有異志，楷諷諭久之，乃就路．楷察秀有悔色，因勒兵為備．秀至興樂，去益州四十餘里，將反襲楷，密使覘之，知不可犯而止．楷在益州，甚有惠政，蜀中父老于今稱之．

translations.literal: In the beginning of Renshou he went out as Commander-in-Chief of Yuanzhou. At that time Prince Xiu of Shu garrisoned Yizhou; the Emperor was about to summon him and hesitated to act. The court feared Xiu would make trouble; Kai was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yizhou and galloped by post to replace him. Xiu indeed had rebellious intent; Kai admonished him for a long time, and he then took the road. Kai saw Xiu had a look of regret and therefore arrayed troops in readiness. Xiu reached Xingle, forty-odd li from Yizhou, and was about to turn and surprise Kai; he secretly sent men to spy and learned he could not be attacked and stopped. Kai in Yizhou had very benevolent government; the elders of Shu to this day praise him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Renshou he became commander-in-chief of Yuanzhou. Prince Xiu of Shu held Yizhou; the emperor meant to recall him but hesitated, fearing revolt. Kai was sent to replace him at post speed. Xiu was indeed disloyal; Kai reasoned with him long until he set out. Seeing regret on Xiu's face, Kai kept his troops ready. At Xingle, forty li from Yizhou, Xiu nearly turned back to ambush him; spies found Kai unassailable and he desisted. Kai ruled Yizhou with real kindness—the elders of Shu still praise him.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，轉赠州總管．遇疾喪明，上表乞骸骨．帝曰：「公先朝舊臣，臥以鎮之，無勞躬親簿領也．」以其長子淩雲監省郡事．其見重如此．轉長平太守．卒，諡曰恭．子淩雲、平雲、彥雲，皆知名．

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Zengzhou. He fell ill and lost his sight, and submitted a memorial begging to retire on account of age. The Emperor said: "You, sir, are an old minister of the former court; lie down to hold the region in peace—there is no need to attend to ledgers in person." His eldest son Lingyun was ordered to oversee the commandery affairs. He was regarded with such esteem. He was transferred to Administrator of Changping. He died; his posthumous title was Gong. His sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun were all well known.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he became commander-in-chief of Zengzhou. Illness took his sight; he asked to retire. The emperor said: "You are an elder of the founding reign—rest and hold the post; do not trouble yourself with accounts." His eldest son Lingyun ran the prefecture in his stead, so highly was he valued. He later served as prefect of Changping, died, and received the posthumous name Gong. Sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun all won notice.

sentences.zh: 獨孤盛

translations.literal: Dugu Sheng
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Sheng

sentences.zh: 楷弟盛，性剛烈，有膽略．以藩邸之舊，累遷右屯纫將軍．宇文化及之亂，裴虔通引兵至成象殿，宿纫者皆釋仗走．盛謂虔通曰：「何物兵？

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Sheng was fierce and resolute, with courage and strategy. Because of old ties from the princely residence he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Right Garrison Guard. In Yuwen Huaji's rebellion, Pei Qiantong led troops to the Chenxiang Hall; the guards of the residence all dropped their weapons and fled. Sheng said to Qiantong: "What sort of soldiers are these?
translations.idiomatic: Kai's brother Sheng was fierce and bold. Old ties from the princely household raised him to general of the right garrison guard. When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, Pei Qiantong marched on Chenxiang Hall and the palace guards threw down their arms and ran. Sheng cried to Qiantong: "What kind of army is this?

sentences.zh: 形勢太異！

translations.literal: The situation is utterly changed!
translations.idiomatic: The whole situation has turned!

sentences.zh: 」虔通曰：「事已然，不預將軍事．」盛罵曰：「老賊，何物語！

translations.literal: " Qiantong said: "The affair is already done; it does not concern the general." Sheng cursed him: "Old thief, what talk is that!
translations.idiomatic: " Qiantong said: "It is already settled—not your affair, general." Sheng raged: "Old villain, what nonsense is that!

sentences.zh: 」不及被甲，與左右十餘人逆拒之，為亂兵所殺．越王侗稱制，贈光祿大夫、紀國公，諡曰武節．

translations.literal: " Before he could don armor, with a dozen or so followers he met them in resistance and was killed by the mutinous troops. Prince of Yue Tong, acting as regent, posthumously awarded him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Duke of the State of Ji, with the posthumous title Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: " He had no time to arm; with a dozen men he stood in their path and the mutineers cut him down. Prince Tong of Yue, holding regency, posthumously made him grand master for splendid happiness and duke of Ji, with the posthumous name Wujie ("martial integrity").

sentences.zh: 乞伏慧

translations.literal: Qi Fuhui
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fuhui

sentences.zh: 乞伏慧字令和，馬邑鮮卑人也．祖周，魏銀青光祿大夫；

translations.literal: Qi Fuhui, styled Linghe, was a Xianbei man of Mayi. His grandfather Zhou was Wei Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness;
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fuhui, courtesy name Linghe, was a Xianbei of Mayi. His grandfather Zhou had been Wei silver-gleaming grand master for splendid happiness;

sentences.zh: 父纂，金紫光祿大夫．並為第一領人酋長．

translations.literal: his father Zuan, Golden-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. Both were chieftains of the first-rank tribal leaders.
translations.idiomatic: his father Zuan, golden-gleaming grand master for splendid happiness. Both had been first-rank tribal chieftains.

sentences.zh: 慧少慷慨，有大節，便弓馬，好鷹犬．齊文襄時，為行臺左丞，累遷太僕卿，自永寧縣公封宜人郡王．[一一]其兄貴和，又以軍功為王．一門二王，稱為貴顯．周武平齊，授使持節、開府儀同大將軍，拜佽飛右旅下大夫，轉熊渠中大夫．從韋孝寬擊尉遲惇於武陟，以功授大將軍．及破尉遲迥，進位柱國，賜爵西河郡公．請以官爵讓兄，朝廷不許，論者義之．

translations.literal: Hui in youth was generous and had great integrity, skilled with bow and horse, fond of hawks and hounds. In the time of Wenxiang of Qi he was Left Director of the Mobile Office, was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Imperial Stud, and from Duke of Yongning County was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiren Commandery. [11] His elder brother Guihe also became a prince through military merit. One family with two princes was called illustrious. When Zhou pacified Qi he was appointed Commissioner with the Staff, Opening Grandee, Grand General with the Same Rites as the Three Dukes, and appointed Lower Grandee of the Right Feiyi Brigade, transferred to Grandee of the Central Bear Brigade. He followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuchi Dun at Wuzhi and through merit was appointed Grand General. When Yuchi Jiong was defeated he was advanced to Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe Commandery. He requested to yield his office and enfeoffment to his elder brother; the court did not permit it, and commentators praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Hui was open-handed and high-minded, skilled in horse and bow and fond of falconry. Under Northern Qi's Wenxiang he rose to left director of the mobile office and director of the imperial stud, from duke of Yongning to prince of Yiren commandery. His brother Guihe won a princedom by arms as well—two kings in one house, the height of honor. When the Zhou conquered Qi he became commissioner with staff, opening grandee, and grand general with three-duke parity, then grandee of the right Feiyi and Bear brigades. He followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuchi Dun at Wuzhi and became grand general; after Jiong's fall he was pillar of state and duke of Xihe. He asked to yield rank and title to his brother; the court refused, and men praised his fairness.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，拜曹州刺史．曹土舊俗，人多姦隱，戶口簿帳，恒不以實．慧下車按察，得戶數萬．遷涼州總管．先是，突厥屢為寇抄，慧嚴警烽燧，遠為斥候，虜竟不入境．後為荊州總管，又領潭桂二州總管、三十一州諸軍事．其俗輕剽，慧躬行朴素以矯之，風化大洽．曾見人以兽捕魚者，出絹買而放之，其仁心如此．百姓美之，號其處曰西河公兽．

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication he was appointed Governor of Caozhou. The old custom of the people of Cao was that many practiced fraud and concealment; household registers and ledgers were constantly not according to fact. When Hui took office he investigated and obtained tens of thousands of households. He was transferred as Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou. Before this the Turks had repeatedly raided and plundered; Hui strictly alerted the beacon fires and set distant scouts, and the barbarians in the end did not enter the territory. Later he was Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou and also concurrently Commander-in-Chief of Tan and Gui Prefectures and military affairs of thirty-one prefectures. The custom there was light and rash; Hui personally practiced simplicity to correct it, and transformation was greatly harmonious. Once he saw men using beasts to catch fish; he produced silk to buy and release them—such was his humane heart. The people praised him and called his place the Western Duke's Beast.
translations.idiomatic: At Wen's accession he became governor of Cao. Cao folk had long hidden households from the rolls; Hui's first audit found tens of thousands unreported. As commander-in-chief of Liangzhou he lit beacons and pushed scouts far out until the Turks ceased to cross the border. He later held Jingzhou and thirty-one prefectures around Tan and Gui. The region was wild and flashy; he lived plainly himself until custom softened. Seeing men fish with otters, he paid silk to free the catch—such was his temper. People nicknamed his district "Lord Xihe's beast" in praise.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，為天水太守．大業五年，征吐谷渾，郡濱西境，人苦勞役，又遇帝西巡，[一二]坐御道不整，獻食疏薄，帝大怒，命左右斬之．見其無髮，乃釋之．除名，卒于家．

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne he was Administrator of Tianshui. In the fifth year of Daye, on the campaign against Tuyuhun, the commandery bordered the western frontier; the people suffered from corvée labor, and moreover encountered the Emperor's western tour. [12] Because the imperial road was not in order and the food offered was sparse, the Emperor was greatly enraged and ordered the attendants to behead him. Seeing that he had no hair, he then released him. His name was struck off; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he was prefect of Tianshui. In Daye 5, on the Tuyuhun campaign, his commandery lay on the western marches; corvée broke the people, and the emperor's western tour found the road ill-kept and his provisions meager. Enraged, Yang ordered him beheaded—then saw he was bald and spared him. Struck from the rolls, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 張威，不知何許人也．父琛，魏弘農太守．

translations.literal: Zhang Wei—is not known from what place. His father Chen was Wei Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei's origin is unrecorded. His father Chen had been Wei prefect of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 威少倜儻，有大志，善騎射，膂力過人．仕周，以軍功位柱國、京兆尹，封長壽縣公．王謙作亂，隋文帝以威為行軍總管，從梁睿擊之．軍次通谷，謙守將李三王拒守．睿以威為先鋒．[一三]三王閉壘不戰，威令人激怒之，三王果出陣．威令壯士奮擊，三王軍潰．大兵繼進至開遠，謙將趙儼红十萬，連營三十里．威鑿山通道，攻其背，儼敗走，追至成都．及謙平，進位上柱國、瀘州總管．

translations.literal: Wei in youth was unconventional and had great ambition, skilled in riding and shooting, with physical strength surpassing others. In Zhou, through military merit he held the rank of Pillar of State and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, enfeoffed as Duke of Changshou County. When Wang Qian rebelled, Emperor Wen of Sui appointed Wei as campaign commander to follow Liang Rui in attacking him. The army halted at Tonggu; Qian's defending general Li Sanwang held the pass. Rui made Wei the vanguard. [13] Sanwang closed the fortress and would not fight; Wei had men provoke him, and Sanwang indeed came out to battle. Wei ordered stalwarts to strike fiercely; Sanwang's army was routed. The great army continued to Kaiyuan; Qian's general Zhao Yan had a hundred thousand troops in connected camps for thirty li. Wei cut a path through the mountain to attack his rear; Yan was defeated and fled, pursued to Chengdu. When Qian was pacified, he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and Commander-in-Chief of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wei was restless and ambitious, a superb rider and archer of uncommon strength. Under the Zhou he became pillar of state and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, duke of Changshou. When Wang Qian rebelled, Wen made him campaign commander under Liang Rui. At Tonggu Pass, Qian's Li Sanwang held the fort; Rui set Wei in the van. Sanwang would not fight until Wei's men taunted him out; stalwarts shattered his line and the main army pressed on to Kaiyuan. Zhao Yan held a hundred thousand men in camps thirty li long; Wei cut a mountain road into his rear, routed him, and chased to Chengdu. After Qian's fall Wei was senior pillar of state and commander-in-chief of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，拜幽、洛二州總管，改封晉熙郡公．尋拜河北道行臺僕射，後督晉王軍府事．遷青州總管．在青州頗事產業，遣家奴於人間鬻蘆菔根，其奴緣此侵擾百姓．上深加譴責，坐廢於家．後從上祠太山，至洛陽，上責讓之，因問威所執笏安在．威頓首曰：「臣負罪，無顏復執，謹藏於家．」上曰：「可持來．」威明日奉笏以見，上曰：「公雖不遵法度，功刋實多，今還公笏．」於是復拜洛州刺史．後改封皖城郡公，轉相州刺史．卒．

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of You and Luo Prefectures and changed to Duke of Jinxi Commandery. Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Hebei Circuit Office, later supervised the Prince of Jin's military headquarters. He was transferred as Commander-in-Chief of Qingzhou. In Qingzhou he quite pursued estates and sent household slaves to sell radish roots among the people; the slaves on this account harassed the common people. The Emperor deeply reproached him and he was punished by dismissal to his home. Later he followed the Emperor in sacrificing at Mount Tai; reaching Luoyang, the Emperor rebuked him and therefore asked where the tablet of office he held was. Wei knocked his head and said: "Your servant bears guilt and has no face to hold it again; I have reverently stored it at home." The Emperor said: "You may bring it." The next day Wei presented the tablet to audience; the Emperor said: "Though you, sir, did not observe law and measure, your recorded merit is indeed great; now I return your tablet." Thereupon he was again appointed Governor of Luozhou. Later he was changed to Duke of Wancheng Commandery and transferred to Governor of Xiangzhou. He died.
translations.idiomatic: At Wen's accession he commanded You and Luo, then became duke of Jinxi, Hebei vice director, and overseer of the Prince of Jin's military house, and finally commander-in-chief of Qingzhou. There he built estates and set slaves to peddle radish—who bullied the people. Wen rebuked him and sent him home. On the Mount Tai rite at Luoyang the emperor asked where his court tablet was. Wei kowtowed: "I am shamed and keep it at home." "Bring it tomorrow," said the emperor; when Wei came with it, Wen said: "You broke the rules, yet your service was great—I return your tablet," and restored him to Luozhou, later Wancheng duke and Xiangzhou governor, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子植，大業中，位至武賁郎將．

translations.literal: His son Zhi, in the Daye era, reached the post of Commandant of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, in the Daye period, became commandant of the martial guard.

sentences.zh: 和洪，汝南人也．勇烈過人．仕周，以軍功位車騎大將軍、儀同三司．時龍州蠻任公忻、李國立等聚红為亂，刺史獨孤善不能禦．朝議以洪有武略，代善為刺史．月餘，斬公忻、國立等，皆平之．後從武帝平齊，位上儀同，賜爵北平侯，拜左勳曹下大夫．柱國王軌之禽吳明徹也，洪有功焉，加位開府，遷折衝中大夫．

translations.literal: He Hong was a man of Runan. His fierce valor surpassed others. In Zhou, through military merit he held the rank of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Yitong of the Third Rank. At that time the Man of Longzhou Ren Gongxin and Li Guoli and others gathered troops in rebellion; Governor Dugu Shan could not repel them. The court discussed that Hong had military strategy and replaced Shan as governor. In a little more than a month he beheaded Gongxin, Guoli, and others; all were pacified. Later he followed Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, held the rank of Upper Yitong, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Beiping, and appointed Lower Grandee of the Left Merit Bureau. When Pillar of State Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche, Hong had merit therein and was advanced to Opening Grandee and transferred to Grandee of the Breaker of Charges.
translations.idiomatic: He Hong came from Runan, fiercer than most. Under the Zhou he was grand general of chariots and cavalry and yitong of the third rank. When Longzhou barbarians Ren Gongxin and Li Guoli rose, Governor Dugu Shan failed; the court sent Hong for his generalship, and within a month he had beheaded the leaders. He followed Emperor Wu against Qi, became upper yitong and marquis of Beiping, and served in the left merit bureau. He helped Wang Gui take Wu Mingche and was made opening grandee and grandee of the breaker of charges.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥作亂，洪以行軍總管從韋孝寬擊之，以功封廣武郡公．時東夏初平，物情尚梗，隋文帝以洪有威名，令領冀州事，甚得人和．後拜泗州刺史．屬突厥寇邊，詔洪為北道行軍總管，擊走之，追虜至磧而還．後遷徐州總管．卒．

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Hong as campaign commander followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him and through merit was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangwu Commandery. At that time eastern Xia was newly pacified and popular sentiment was still resistant; Emperor Wen of Sui, because Hong had a famous reputation, ordered him to oversee Jizhou affairs and greatly won human harmony. Later he was appointed Governor of Sizhou. When the Turks raided the frontier, by edict Hong was campaign commander of the northern route, attacked and drove them off, pursued the barbarians to the desert and returned. Later he was transferred as Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou. He died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuchi Jiong's rebellion he campaigned under Wei Xiaokuan and was made duke of Guangwu. Eastern territories were still unsettled; Wen set him over Jizhou for his name and won the people's hearts. He governed Sizhou, then as northern-route commander drove off a Turk raid and chased them into the desert. He ended as commander-in-chief of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陰壽字羅雲，武威人也．父嵩，周夏州刺史．

translations.literal: Yin Shou, styled Luoyun, was a native of Wuwei. His father Song was Zhou Governor of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shou, courtesy name Luoyun, came from Wuwei. His father Song had been Zhou governor of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 壽少果烈，有武幹，性謹厚．從周武帝平齊，位開府．隋文帝為丞相，引為掾．尉遲迥亂，文帝以韋孝寬為元帥擊之，命壽監軍．時孝寬有疾，不能親總戎事，每臥帳中，遣婦人傳教命，三軍綱紀，皆取決於壽．以功進位上柱國．尋拜幽州總管，封趙郡公．

translations.literal: Shou in youth was resolute and fierce, with military capacity; his nature was careful and thick. He followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Qi and held the rank of Opening Grandee. When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, he was brought in as an aide. In Yuchi Jiong's disorder the Emperor appointed Wei Xiaokuan as commander-in-chief to attack him and ordered Shou to supervise the army. At that time Xiaokuan was ill and could not personally command the army affairs; each time lying in the tent, he sent women to transmit orders and teach commands—the three armies' discipline all depended on Shou. Through merit he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State. Soon he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shou in youth was decisive and martial yet careful by nature. He followed Emperor Wu of Zhou against Qi and became opening grandee. When Wen was regent he entered his staff. In Jiong's revolt Wen set Wei Xiaokuan over the army and Shou to supervise it. Xiaokuan lay ill in his tent and sent women with his orders; discipline rested entirely on Shou. For this he became senior pillar of state and commander-in-chief of Youzhou, duke of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊之疏屬高寶寧，周武帝拜為營州刺史，性桀黠，得華夷心．及文帝為丞相，遂連契丹、靺鞨舉兵反．帝以中原多故，未遑進討，諭之不下．開皇初，又引突厥圍北平．至是，令壽討之．寶寧棄城奔于磧北，黃龍諸縣悉平．壽班師，留開府成道昂鎮之．壽患寶寧攻道昂，乃重購獲之，北邊遂安．卒官，贈司空．

translations.literal: Before this, Gao Baoning, a distant kinsman of Qi, whom Emperor Wu of Zhou had appointed Governor of Yingzhou, was fierce and cunning and had won the hearts of Chinese and barbarians alike. When the Emperor was Chancellor he then linked the Khitan and Mohe and raised troops in rebellion. The Emperor, because the central plains had many affairs and could not yet advance to attack, admonished him but he would not submit. In the beginning of Kaihuang he again led the Turks to besiege Beiping. At this time he ordered Shou to attack him. Baoning abandoned the city and fled to the desert north; the counties of Huanglong were all pacified. Shou withdrew the army and left Opening Grandee Cheng Da'ang to garrison it. Shou feared Baoning would attack Da'ang and therefore offered a heavy reward and captured him; the northern frontier was then at peace. He died in office and was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baoning of Qi, a distant kinsman whom Emperor Wu had made governor of Yingzhou, was sly and had won both Chinese and tribes. When Wen was regent, Baoning joined Khitan and Mohe in revolt; Wen could not yet march against him and his warnings failed. In early Kaihuang he brought Turks to besiege Beiping. Shou was sent against him; Baoning fled north of the desert and Huanglong counties were pacified. Shou withdrew, leaving Cheng Da'ang to hold the ground, then bought Baoning's capture when he threatened Da'ang. The north settled. Shou died in post and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 陰世師

translations.literal: Yin Shishi
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shishi

sentences.zh: 子世師，少有節概，性忠厚，多武藝．以功臣子拜儀同．煬帝嗣位，拜張掖太守，深為戎狄所憚．後拜樓煩太守，遷左翊纫將軍，與代王留守京師．及義軍至，世師自以世荷隋恩，遂拒守不下．及城平，與京兆郡丞骨儀等見誅．

translations.literal: His son Shishi in youth had integrity and mettle, a nature loyal and thick, with many martial arts. As the son of a meritorious minister he was appointed Yitong. When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed Governor of Zhangye and was deeply feared by the frontier barbarians. Later he was appointed Governor of Loufan, transferred to General of the Left Flank Guard, and with the Prince of Dai remained to guard the capital. When the righteous army arrived, Shishi, because his family had received Sui grace for generations, therefore held firm and would not surrender. When the city fell, he and the Metropolitan Assistant Gu Yi and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi was young but principled, loyal, and skilled in arms; as a meritorious son he became yitong. Under Emperor Yang he was governor of Zhangye and feared on the frontier, then of Loufan, then left-flank guard general, guarding Chang'an with the Prince of Dai. When Li Yuan's army came, Shishi held the city for Sui's long favor to his house. When it fell he and metropolitan aide Gu Yi were executed.

sentences.zh: 骨儀，天竺胡人．性剛鯁，有不可奪之志．開皇初，為御史，處法平當，不為勢利所迴．煬帝嗣位，遷尚書左司郎．于時朝政漸亂，貨賄公行，凡當樞要之職，無問貴賤，並家累金寶．天下士大夫莫不變節，而儀勵志守常，介然獨立．帝嘉其清苦，拜京兆郡丞，公方彌著．時刑部尚書纫玄兼領京兆內史，[一四]頗行詭道，輒為儀所執正．玄雖不便之，不能傷．及義兵至，玄恐禍及，辭老病．儀與世師同心協契，父子並誅，其後絕．世師有子弘智等，各以年幼獲全．

translations.literal: Gu Yi was a Hu man of Tianzhu. His nature was firm and upright, with a will that could not be wrested away. In the beginning of Kaihuang he was a censor; in applying the law he was fair and even and was not turned by power and profit. When Emperor Yang succeeded he was transferred to Left Director of the Department of State. At that time court government gradually fell into disorder; bribes walked openly; every post holding the pivot, without distinction of noble or base, all accumulated gold and treasure at home. Scholars and officials throughout the realm none did not change their principles, while Yi encouraged his will and kept to constancy, standing alone with integrity. The Emperor praised his pure hardship and appointed him Metropolitan Assistant of Jingzhao; public rectitude became still more marked. At that time Minister of Punishments Wei Xuan concurrently held the metropolitan governorship. [14] He quite practiced devious ways and was often seized and corrected by Yi. Xuan though inconvenienced could not harm him. When the righteous army arrived, Xuan feared disaster would reach him and pleaded old age and illness. Yi and Shishi were of one mind in their covenant; father and son were both executed, and thereafter the line ended. Shishi had sons Hongzhi and others; each because of young age was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yi was an Indian Hu, iron in character and unbending. In early Kaihuang he was a censor, fair and unmoved by power. Under Emperor Yang he was left director of state while the court rotted and bribes ran open; every man at the center heaped up gold, and gentry everywhere bent—yet Yi held his course alone. The emperor prized his austerity and made him metropolitan aide of Jingzhao. Minister of punishments Wei Xuan also governed the capital and loved crooked paths; Yi corrected him repeatedly and Xuan could not touch him. When the righteous army came, Xuan feigned age and illness. Yi and Shishi stood together; both were killed and the line ended, though Shishi's young sons Hongzhi and the rest were spared.

sentences.zh: 楊義臣

translations.literal: Yang Yichen
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yichen

sentences.zh: 楊義臣，代人也，本姓尉遲氏．父崇，仕周，為儀同大將軍，以兵鎮恒山．時隋文帝為定州總管，崇知帝相貌非常，每自結納，帝甚親待之．及為丞相，尉遲迥亂，崇以宗族故，自囚，遣使請罪．帝下書慰諭之，即令馳驛入朝，恒置左右．開皇初，封秦興公．歲餘，從行軍總管達奚長儒擊突厥於周槃，力戰而死．贈大將軍、豫州刺史，以義臣襲崇官爵．

translations.literal: Yang Yichen was a man of Dai; his original surname was Yuchi. His father Chong, serving Zhou, was Grand General, Yitong of the Third Rank, and with troops garrisoned Hengshan. At that time Emperor Wen of Sui was Commander-in-Chief of Dingzhou; Chong knew the Emperor's appearance was extraordinary and each time personally formed ties with him; the Emperor was very intimate with him. When he became Chancellor, in Yuchi Jiong's disorder Chong because of clan ties imprisoned himself and sent envoys to request punishment. The Emperor issued a letter comforting and instructing him, and immediately ordered him to come by post-horse to court, always placing him at his side. In the beginning of Kaihuang he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinxing. After more than a year he followed Campaign Commander Daxi Changru in attacking the Turks at Zhoupan, fought fiercely, and died. He was posthumously awarded Grand General and Governor of Yuzhou; Yichen inherited Chong's office and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yichen came from Dai; his clan had been Yuchi. His father Chong, a Zhou grand general yitong of the third rank, held Hengshan. When the future Emperor Wen was commander-in-chief of Dingzhou, Chong saw his extraordinary bearing and courted him; they were close. When Wen became regent and Jiong rebelled, Chong, as kin, imprisoned himself and asked punishment; Wen comforted him and called him to court by post, keeping him always near. In early Kaihuang he was duke of Qinxing. A year later he followed Daxi Changru at Zhoupan against the Turks, fought to the death, and was posthumously made grand general and governor of Yuzhou; Yichen inherited his rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 時義臣尚幼，養於宮中，未弱冠，奉詔宿纫如千牛者數年，賞賜甚厚．上嘗言及恩舊，顧義臣嗟嘆久之，因下詔賜義臣姓楊氏，編之屬籍，為皇從孫．未幾，拜陝州刺史．義臣性謹厚，能騎射，有將領才．後突厥達頭可汗犯塞，以行軍總管出白道，大破之．明年，突厥又寇邊，義臣擊之，追至大斤山，與虜遇．時太平公史萬歲亦至，與義臣合擊大破之．萬歲為楊素所陷，義臣功竟不錄．

translations.literal: At that time Yichen was still young and was raised in the palace; before reaching capped age, by edict he lodged in the guard like the thousand bulls for several years, with rewards very thick. The Emperor once spoke of old grace, looked at Yichen and sighed for a long time, and therefore issued an edict granting Yichen the surname Yang, enrolling him in the imperial clan as imperial cousin from afar. Before long he was appointed Governor of Shanzhou. Yichen's nature was careful and thick; he could ride and shoot and had the talent of a commander. Later the Turkic khan Datou violated the frontier; as campaign commander he went out by the Baidao and greatly defeated them. The next year the Turks again raided the frontier; Yichen attacked them, pursued to Mount Dajin, and met the barbarians. At that time Duke of Peace Shi Wansui also arrived; together with Yichen they joined attack and greatly defeated them. Wansui was trapped by Yang Su; Yichen's merit in the end was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen was still a boy, reared in the palace; before his capping he lodged with the guard like the thousand-bull cadets for years on rich bounty. Wen once spoke of old favors, looked at him long, and granted him the Yang surname and a place among the imperial cousins. Soon he was governor of Shanzhou—careful, able in horse and bow, a born commander. Datou raided; Yichen went out the Baidao and crushed him. The next year he chased the Turks to Mount Dajin, where Shi Wansui joined him and they broke the enemy together. Su destroyed Wansui; Yichen's honors were buried with him.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒反．時代州總管李景被諒將喬鍾葵所圍，義臣時為朔州總管，奉詔救之．鍾葵見義臣兵少，悉红拒之．時鍾葵亞將王拔驍勇，善用桕，射者不能中，每以數騎陷陣．義臣患之，募能當拔者．有車騎將軍楊思恩請當之．義臣見思恩氣貌雄勇，顧之曰：「壯士也！

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Prince of Han Liang rebelled. At that time Commander-in-Chief of Daizhou Li Jing was besieged by Liang's general Qiao Zhongkui; Yichen was then Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou and by edict went to rescue him. Zhongkui saw Yichen's troops were few and gathered all his troops to resist him. At that time Zhongkui's second-in-command Wang Ba was fierce and brave, skilled in using the staff; archers could not hit him, and each time with several horsemen he broke the array. Yichen was troubled by him and recruited one who could meet Ba. Cavalry General Yang Si'en requested to take him on. Yichen saw Si'en's spirit and appearance were heroic and brave, and looked at him, saying: "A stalwart!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Prince Liang of Han rebelled. Li Jing of Daizhou was besieged by Liang's Qiao Zhongkui; Yichen, then commander-in-chief of Shuozhou, was ordered to relieve him. Zhongkui saw few troops and massed his whole force. Zhongkui's lieutenant Wang Ba was a terror with the staff—archers could not touch him, and with a handful of horse he pierced the line. Yichen sought a man to meet him; cavalry general Yang Si'en volunteered. Yichen looked at his bold bearing and said: "A true champion!

sentences.zh: 」賜以墒酒．思恩望見拔立於陣後，投觴於地，策馬赴之．再往不剋，所從騎士退，思恩為拔所殺．拔遂乘之，義臣軍北者十餘里．於是購得思恩屍，義臣哭之甚慟，三軍莫不下泣，所從騎士皆腰斬．義臣自以兵少，悉取軍中牛驢，得數千頭，復令數百人，人持一鼓，潛驅之诙谷間，出其不意．義臣晡後復與鍾葵戰，兵初合，命驅牛驢者疾進．一時鳴鼓，埃塵張天，鍾葵軍不知所以，以為伏兵發，因大潰，縱擊破之．以功進位上大將軍．累遷太僕卿．

translations.literal: " He gave him strong wine. Si'en saw Ba standing behind the array, threw his cup to the ground, and spurred toward him. Twice he went and did not overcome him; the horsemen who followed retreated, and Si'en was killed by Ba. Ba then rode over him; Yichen's army was driven north more than ten li. Thereupon he purchased Si'en's corpse; Yichen wept for him extremely bitterly, and the three armies all bowed their heads and wept; the horsemen who had followed were all cut in two at the waist. Yichen himself because his troops were few took all the oxen and donkeys in the army, obtaining several thousand head, and again ordered several hundred men, each holding a drum, to drive them secretly through the Huangu Valley and come out where they did not expect. Yichen in the afternoon again fought with Zhongkui; when the troops first joined, he ordered those driving the oxen and donkeys to advance quickly. At once they beat the drums; dust filled the sky; Zhongkui's army did not know why, thought ambush troops had risen, and therefore was greatly routed; he released pursuit and broke them. Through merit he was advanced to Senior Grand General. He was repeatedly transferred to Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him strong wine. Si'en saw Ba behind the line, dashed his cup down, and charged. Twice he failed; his riders fell back and Ba killed him and rode over the body. Yichen's line was driven ten li north. He ransomed Si'en's corpse and wept until the whole army wept; the riders who had retreated were cut in two at the waist. Too few to fight head-on, he took every ox and donkey in camp—thousands—and hid hundreds of men with drums in Huangu Valley. That afternoon he met Zhongkui again; as the lines met, the drivers rushed forward and every drum sounded at once. Dust blotted the sky; Zhongkui thought ambush and broke. Yichen routed him and was made senior grand general, then director of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，令義臣屯琵琶峽，連營八十里，南接元壽，北連段文振，合圍吐谷渾主於覆袁川．復從征遼東，以軍將指肅慎道．至鴨綠水，與乙支文德戰，每為先鋒，一日七捷．後與諸軍俱敗，竟坐免．俄而復位．明年，以為軍副，與大將軍宇文述趣平壤．至鴨綠水，會楊玄感作亂班師，檢校趙郡太守．妖賊向海公作亂，寇扶風、安定間，[一五]義臣奉詔擊平之．尋從帝復征遼東，進位左光祿大夫．

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Tuyuhun and was ordered to garrison at Pipa Gorge, connecting camps for eighty li, south joining Yuan Shou, north joining Duan Wenzhen, jointly surrounding the Tuyuhun ruler at Fuyuan River. He again followed the campaign against Liaodong, as army commander directing the Sushhen route. Reaching the Yalu River, he fought with Ye Zhishiwen; each time he was vanguard, seven victories in one day. Later he was defeated along with the other armies and was punished by dismissal. Before long he was restored to office. The next year he was made deputy commander; with Grand General Yuwen Shu he advanced on Pyongyang. Reaching the Yalu River, they met Yang Xuangan's rebellion and withdrew the army; he was inspecting Administrator of Zhao Commandery. The demonic bandit Xiang Hai'gong rebelled, raiding between Fufeng and Anding. [15] Yichen by edict attacked and pacified him. Soon he followed the Emperor again on the Liaodong campaign and was advanced to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign he held Pipa Gorge in an eighty-li chain of camps, joining Yuan Shou to the south and Duan Wenzhen to the north to pen the khan at Fuyuan River. On Liaodong he led the Sushhen route to the Yalu and fought Ye Zhishiwen seven times as vanguard in a single day. When the armies failed he was dismissed, soon restored, then made deputy to Yuwen Shu against Pyongyang; at the Yalu, Xuangan's revolt turned them back and he became inspecting prefect of Zhao. The outlaw Xiang Hai'gong troubled Fufeng and Anding; Yichen crushed him by edict, followed Yang on Liaodong again, and was made left grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 時勃海高士達、清河張金稱並相聚為盜，攻陷郡縣．帝遣將軍段達討之，不能剋，詔義臣率遼東還兵擊之，[一六]大破士達，斬金稱．又收降賊，入豆子隲，討賊格謙禽之，以狀聞奏．帝惡其威名，遽追入朝，賊由是復盛．義臣以功進位光祿大夫，尋拜禮部尚書．卒于官．

translations.literal: At that time Gao Shida of Bohai and Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe both gathered and became bandits, attacking and taking prefectures and counties. The Emperor sent General Duan Da to attack them and he could not overcome them; by edict Yichen led the Liaodong-returning troops to attack them, [16] greatly defeated Shida, and beheaded Jincheng. He again received the surrender of bandits, entered Douzi Mire, attacked the bandit Ge Qian and captured him, and reported the facts in a memorial. The Emperor hated his famous prestige and hastily recalled him to court; the bandits therefore flourished again. Yichen through merit was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; soon he was appointed Minister of Rites. He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shida of Bohai and Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe had become bandit kings, taking counties the court could not recover until Duan Da failed and Yichen was sent with the Liaodong veterans to break Shida and behead Jincheng. He accepted surrenders, entered Douzi Mire, and took Ge Qian—but the emperor feared his fame and recalled him at once, and the rebels swelled again. He rose to grand master for splendid happiness and minister of rites, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：昔韓信愆垓下之期，則項王不滅；

translations.literal: The commentary says: In old times Han Xin missed the appointment below Gaixia, and the King of Xiang was not destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: In antiquity Han Xin broke his rendezvous below Gaixia, and Lord Xiang was not destroyed;

sentences.zh: 英布無淮南之舉，則漢道未隆．以二子之勳庸，咸憤怨而葅戮，況乃無古人之殊績，而懷悖逆之心者乎！

translations.literal: Ying Bu made no rising in Huainan, and the Han way was not yet exalted. With the merit and achievement of these two men, both harbored resentment and were minced alive—how much more those who had no extraordinary merit of the ancients yet harbored rebellious hearts!
translations.idiomatic: Ying Bu never rose in Huainan, and the Han mandate had not yet soared. Those two, for all their service, died resentful and dismembered—what of men with no such deeds who yet nursed treason?

sentences.zh: 梁士彥遭雲雷之會，以勇略成名，遂貪天之功以為己力．報者倦矣，施者未厭，將生厲階，求逞其欲．及茲顛墜，自取之也．元諧、虞慶則、元冑，或契闊艱危，或綢繆恩舊，將安將樂，漸見遺忘，內懷怏怏，矜伐不已．雖時主之刻薄，亦言語以速禍乎！

translations.literal: Liang Shiyan encountered the meeting of cloud and thunder, made a name through courage and strategy, and then took heaven's achievement as his own strength. The repayer grows weary, the giver not yet sated; he will breed trouble and seek to satisfy his desires. When he falls at this time, he has brought it on himself. Yuan Xie, Yu Qingze, and Yuan Zhou—some shared hardship in danger, some were bound by old grace in intimate friendship; whether about to be secure or joyful, they were gradually forgotten, harboring resentment inwardly, boasting and plundering without end. Though the ruler of the time was harsh and thin, was it not also speech that hastened disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan rode a stormy age to fame by courage, then treated heaven's gift as his own due. When givers tire and receivers still want more, trouble follows. His fall was his own doing. Yuan Xie, Yu Qingze, and Yuan Zhou—some had shared danger, some old intimacy—were forgotten as ease came, grew sullen, and vaunted themselves without end. The emperor was harsh, yet did not their own tongues hurry the blade?

sentences.zh: 然隋文佐命元功，鮮有終其天命，配享清廟，寂爾無聞．斯蓋草創帝圖，事出權道，本異同心，故久而愈薄．其牽牛蹊田，雖則有罪，奪之非道，能無怨乎？

translations.literal: Yet among Emperor Wen of Sui's founding ministers who aided the mandate, few completed their heaven-allotted span, shared sacrifice in the clear temple, and are heard of in silence. This is because in founding an imperial design affairs come from expedient ways, fundamentally different from sharing one heart—therefore over time they grow thinner. Their leading an ox across the field, though there was guilt, yet to seize it by unrighteous means—can there be no resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Of Wen's founding companions, few died in their beds or entered the royal temple—mostly they fade unheard. Founding a throne trades in expedients, not in one heart forever; favor thins with time. Like the man who led his ox across another's field: there was fault, but seizure without right breeds lasting grievance.

sentences.zh: 皆深文巧詆，致之刑辟，帝沈猜之心，固已甚矣．求其餘慶，不亦雖哉！

translations.literal: All were prosecuted with deep words and crafty slander, brought to penal law; the Emperor's deep suspicious heart was already very strong. To seek their remaining blessing—is it not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: All were caught by twisted words and clever indictments; the emperor's suspicion was already deep. To expect their houses further favor—was that not vain?

sentences.zh: 長儒以步卒二千，抗十萬之红，師殲矢盡，勇氣彌厲，壯矣哉！

translations.literal: Changru with two thousand foot soldiers resisted a hundred thousand troops; the army was destroyed and arrows exhausted, yet courage grew fiercer—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Changru with two thousand foot faced a hundred thousand; his army died and his arrows ran out, yet his spirit only burned brighter—how magnificent!

sentences.zh: 子幹西涉青海，北臨玄塞，胡夷懾憚，亦有可稱．萬歲實懷智勇，善撫士卒，人皆樂死，師不疲勞．北劔匈奴，南平夷獠，兵鋒所指，威警絕域．論功仗氣，犯忤貴臣，偏聽生奸，死非其罪，人皆痛惜，有李廣之風焉．劉方號令無私，臨軍嚴肅，克翦林邑，遂清南海，徼外百蠻，無思不服．杜彥東夏南服，屢有戰功，作鎮朔垂，胡塵不起．周搖以質真見知．獨孤楷以恤人流譽．盛蹈履之地，可以追蹤古人．[一七]乞伏慧能以國讓，亦云美矣．而慧以供帳不厚，至於放黜，君方逞欲，罰亦深哉！

translations.literal: Zigan crossed west to Qinghai, north to the dark frontier; the Hu and barbarians feared and respected him, and there is also praise. Wansui truly harbored wisdom and courage, was good at comforting soldiers; men all rejoiced to die for him, and the army was not weary. North he pierced the Xiongnu, south he pacified the Man and Liao; wherever his military edge pointed, prestige and warning reached beyond the borders. Discussing merit and relying on spirit, he offended great ministers; partial listening bred treachery, and he died not for his crime—men all grieved and pitied him, having the manner of Li Guang. Liu Fang's orders were without selfishness; facing the army he was stern and solemn; he cut down Lin Yi and cleared the southern sea; beyond the marches the hundred Man all thought of submission without rebellion. Du Yan in eastern Xia and southern submission repeatedly had military merit; garrisoning the northern frontier, Hu dust did not rise. Zhou Yao was known for his plain authenticity. Dugu Kai was famed for cherishing the people. Sheng, in the ground he trod, can be traced to the ancients. [17] Qi Fuhui could yield the state to others—this too is praised. Yet Hui because the supply train was not thick was banished—the ruler indulging his desires, the punishment also deep!
translations.idiomatic: Zigan ranged west to Qinghai and north to the dark passes; the tribes feared him—rightly praised. Wansui had true genius and loved his men; they died gladly and never tired. He pierced the north and pacified the south; his name alone shook the frontier. Counting his merit and standing proud, he crossed great ministers; the court listened to one side, and he died wrongfully—all China mourned him in Li Guang's way. Fang was selfless in command, stern in camp, cut Lin Yi, and cleared the southern sea until the hundred Yue submitted. Yan won repeated honors in east and south and on the northern wall no dust rose. Yao was prized for plain integrity; Kai for cherishing the people. Sheng, in the ground he stood on, may be set beside the ancients. Hui, who would yield rank to his brother, was also beautiful—yet for thin provisioning at court he was cast off while the ruler's appetite ran wide; harsh indeed.

sentences.zh: 陰世師遭天所廢，舍命無改，[一八]雖異先覺，頗同後凋．義臣時屬擾攘，功成三捷，而以功見忌，得沒亦為幸也．

translations.literal: Yin Shishi was abandoned by heaven yet would not change his life, [18] though different from foreknowing, quite like the late steadfast. Yichen in a time of turmoil achieved merit in three victories, yet because of merit was regarded with jealousy—to die undestroyed was also fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi, abandoned by heaven, would not alter his loyalty—unlike those who see ahead, yet kin to those who stand firm at the end. Yichen in troubled times thrice victorious, then envied for that victory—to fall only in rank and not in life was fortune enough.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: [一] 及齊平封郕國公位上柱國 按周書卷八靜帝紀，梁士彥進上柱國在大象二年十二月，即破尉遲迥之後．此在齊亡之後，破迥之前，疑當是進柱國．

translations.literal: [1] When Qi was pacified he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Xing and appointed Senior Pillar of State. According to the Annals of Emperor Jing in Book of Zhou 8, Liang Shiyan's advancement to Senior Pillar of State was in the twelfth month of the second year of Daxiang, after defeating Yuchi Jiong. This is after Qi's fall and before Jiong's defeat; it should be advancement to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Note 1: The text places Liang Shiyan's enfeoffment as Duke of Xing and appointment as senior pillar of state at the fall of Qi, before the defeat of Yuchi Jiong. Zhou shu 8 dates his senior pillar rank to Daxiang year 2, month 12, after Jiong's defeat. The entry likely should read pillar of state, not senior pillar.

sentences.zh: [二] 為行軍總管及韋孝寬擊之 隋書卷四０、通志卷一六一梁士彥傳「及」作「從」，是．

translations.literal: [2] As campaign commander and with Wei Xiaokuan attacking him. Sui shu 40 and Tong zhi 161 Liang Shiyan biography read "followed" for "and," which is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Note 2: For "as campaign commander and Wei Xiaokuan attacked him," Sui shu 40 and Tong zhi 161 read "followed Wei Xiaokuan," which is correct.

sentences.zh: [三] 時吐谷渾將定城王鐘利旁率騎度河 隋書卷四０元諧傳「旁」作「房」．按本書卷九六、隋書卷八三吐谷渾傳亦作「房」．

translations.literal: [3] At that time the Tuyuhun general Dingcheng Wang Zhonglifang led cavalry across the river. Sui shu 40 Yuan Xie biography reads "fang" for "pang." This book 96 and Sui shu 83 Tuyuhun biography also read "fang."
translations.idiomatic: Note 3: The Tuyuhun general is named Zhonglifang of Dingcheng in Sui shu 40 Yuan Xie; other texts read fang rather than pang, as in Beishi 96 and Sui shu 83.

sentences.zh: [四] 諧率兵出鄯州 諸本脫「諧」字，據隋書補．

translations.literal: [4] Xie led troops out of Shanzhou. Various editions omit the character "Xie"; supplied according to Sui shu.
translations.idiomatic: Note 4: "Led troops out of Shanzhou" omits Xie in some editions; restored from Sui shu.

sentences.zh: [五] 歸桂鎮 隋書卷四０虞慶則傳作「至潭州臨桂鎮」．通志卷一六一虞慶則傳作「還臨桂鎮」．通鑑卷一七八五五五九頁作「至潭州臨桂嶺」．疑此脫「臨」字．

translations.literal: [5] Returned to garrison Gui. Sui shu 40 Yu Qingze biography reads "reached Tanzhou at Lingui garrison." Tong zhi 161 reads "returned to Lingui garrison." Zizhi tongjian 178 reads "reached Tanzhou at Lingui ridge." This text perhaps omits lin.
translations.idiomatic: Note 5: "Returned to garrison Gui"—Sui shu 40 has "reached Tanzhou, Lingui garrison"; Tong zhi 161 "returned to Lingui garrison"; Zizhi tongjian 178 "Lingui ridge." Lin may be lost here.

sentences.zh: [六] 及藩那可汗寇掠而南 諸本「而南」作「西南」．按突厥在隋之北，不得云「寇掠西南」．隋書卷五三達奚長儒傳「西」作「而」是，今據改．

translations.literal: [6] And the dependent khan Fan raided southward. Various editions read "southwest" for "south." The Turks were north of Sui and could not be said to raid the southwest. Sui shu 53 Daxi Changru biography reads "er" for "xi," which is correct; amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note 6: Editions read "southwest" for south; Turks lay north of Sui. Sui shu 53 Daxi Changru has er, not xi—amended here.

sentences.zh: [七] 以思安縣伯別封子皎 諸本「思」作「忠」，隋書卷五三賀婁子幹傳作「思」．按上文言子幹封思安縣子，進爵為伯．「忠」字訛，今據改．

translations.literal: [7] The Si'an county barony separately enfeoffed on his son Jiao. Various editions read "zhong" for "si"; Sui shu 53 Helou Zigan reads "si." Above it says Zigan was enfeoffed Viscount of Si'an and advanced to Baron. "Zhong" is erroneous; amended according to Sui shu.
translations.idiomatic: Note 7: "Si'an county barony to son Jiao"—some texts write zhong for si; Sui shu 53 has si, matching the earlier Si'an viscountcy.

sentences.zh: [八] 度西二河 通志卷一六一史萬歲傳作「西弭河」，通鑑卷一七八五五五一頁作「西洱河」．胡注引蘇軾曰：「南詔有西洱河，河形如月抱珥，故名之為西洱河．」這裏作「西二」，當是音近致訛．

translations.literal: [8] Crossed the two western rivers. Tong zhi 161 Shi Wansui reads "west Mi River"; Zizhi tongjian 178 reads "west Er River." Su Shi notes that Nanzhao has a West Er River shaped like the moon embracing an ear, hence the name. "West two" here is likely a sound error.
translations.idiomatic: Note 8: "Crossed the two western rivers"—Tong zhi 161 has west Mi River; Zizhi tongjian 178 west Er River. Su Shi says Nanzhao's West Er River is named for its moon-and-ear shape; "west two" is likely a phonetic error.

sentences.zh: [九] 方親帥大將軍張愻司馬李綱舟師趣北境 隋書卷五三、通志卷一六一劉方傳及通鑑卷一八０五六一六頁「北境」作「比景」．通鑑胡注云：「比景，漢縣，屬日南郡．隋置比景郡見隋書地理志下．」「北境」疑為「比景」之訛．

translations.literal: [9] Fang personally led the great general Zhang Xun, Marshal Li Gang, and the fleet toward the northern border. Sui shu 53, Tong zhi 161 Liu Fang, and Zizhi tongjian 180 read "Bijing" for "northern border." The Hu note: Bijing was a Han county in Rinan commandery; Sui set Bijing commandery—see Sui shu geography. "Northern border" is likely error for Bijing.
translations.idiomatic: Note 9: A sentence on Fang leading Zhang Xun and Li Gang's fleet "toward the northern border" appears in some apparatus; Sui shu 53, Tong zhi 161, and Zizhi tongjian 180 read Bijing, a Han and Sui place in the far south—not the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: [一０]數以行軍總管領邊 隋書卷五三劉方傳附陳永貴，「領」作「鎮」，是．

translations.literal: [10] Several times as campaign commander leading the frontier. Sui shu 53 Liu Fang biography appendix Chen Yonggui reads "garrisoned" for "led," which is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Note 10: "Several times as campaign commander leading the frontier"—Sui shu 53 appendix Chen Yonggui reads garrisoned, which fits.

sentences.zh: [一一]自永寧縣公封宜人郡王 隋書卷五五乞伏慧傳「人」作「民」．北史避唐諱改．

translations.literal: [11] From Duke of Yongning County enfeoffed Prince of Yiren Commandery. Sui shu 55 Qi Fuhui reads "min" for "ren." Beishi avoids Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Note 11: Prince of Yiren—Sui shu 55 has Yimin; Beishi avoids the Tang taboo on min.

sentences.zh: [一二]又遇帝西巡 諸本脫「西」字，據隋書卷五五、通志卷一六一乞伏慧傳補．事見本書卷十二隋煬帝紀大業五年．

translations.literal: [12] Moreover encountered the Emperor's western tour. Various editions omit "west"; supplied from Sui shu 55 and Tong zhi 161. The event is in Beishi 12, Sui Yangdi ji, Daye 5.
translations.idiomatic: Note 12: "Encountered the emperor's western tour"—west is missing in some editions; restored from Sui shu 55 and Tong zhi 161 (Beishi 12, Daye 5).

sentences.zh: [一三]睿以威為先鋒 諸本脫「威」字，據隋書卷五五、通志卷一六一張威傳補．

translations.literal: [13] Rui made Wei the vanguard. Various editions omit "Wei"; supplied from Sui shu 55 and Tong zhi 161 Zhang Wei biography.
translations.idiomatic: Note 13: "Rui made Wei vanguard"—Wei is omitted in some texts; restored from Sui shu 55 and Tong zhi 161.

sentences.zh: [一四]時刑部尚書纫玄兼領京兆內史 諸本「內史」上有「拜」字，隋書卷三九陰壽附骨儀傳無．按隋煬帝改官名，京兆、河南置內史見隋書百官志下．又隋書卷六三纫玄傳，玄於隋末為京兆內史．「拜」字衍文，今據刪．

translations.literal: [14] At that time Minister of Punishments Wei Xuan concurrently held the metropolitan governorship. Various editions have "appointed" before "metropolitan governor"; Sui shu 39 Yin Shou appendix Gu Yi has none. Sui shu 63 Wei Xuan was metropolitan governor at the end of Sui. "Appointed" is superfluous; deleted accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note 14: "Wei Xuan concurrently metropolitan governor"—some texts add appointed before metropolitan governor; Sui shu 39 Gu Yi appendix and Sui shu 63 do not. Deleted as redundant.

sentences.zh: [一五]妖賊向海公作亂寇扶風安定間 按本書卷十二隋煬帝紀、隋書卷四煬帝紀下，大業九年十二月，作「扶風人向海明」，通鑑卷一八二五六八七頁也作向海明．疑「公」字訛．但隋書卷六三、通志卷一六一楊義臣傳亦作「公」，今不改．

translations.literal: [15] The demonic bandit Xiang Hai'gong rebelled and raided between Fufeng and Anding. Beishi 12 and Sui shu 4 Yangdi ji, ninth month of Daye 9, read "Fufeng man Xiang Haiming"; Zizhi tongjian 182 also Xiang Haiming. "Gong" may be error, but Sui shu 63 and Tong zhi 161 Yang Yichen also read gong; left unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Note 15: "Bandit Xiang Hai'gong"—annals (Beishi 12, Sui shu 4, Daye 9) have Fufeng man Xiang Haiming; Zizhi tongjian 182 agrees. Gong may be wrong, yet Sui shu 63 and Tong zhi 161 keep gong—unchanged here.

sentences.zh: [一六]詔義臣率遼東還兵擊之 諸本脫「之」字，據隋書、通志楊義臣傳補．

translations.literal: [16] By edict Yichen led the Liaodong-returning troops to attack them. Various editions omit the final "them"; supplied from Sui shu and Tong zhi Yang Yichen biography.
translations.idiomatic: Note 16: "Led the Liaodong-returning troops to attack them"—final them missing in some editions; restored from Sui shu and Tong zhi.

sentences.zh: [一七]盛蹈履之地可以追蹤古人 諸本「盛」作「威」．按張威本傳行事與此評語不類．獨孤盛死於江都之變，按封建道德標準，認為值得讚揚，故有此評．此乃形似致訛，今改正．

translations.literal: [17] Sheng, in the ground he trod, can be traced to the ancients. Various editions read "Wei" for "Sheng." Zhang Wei's deeds in his own biography do not match this praise. Dugu Sheng died in the Jiangdu mutiny; by feudal moral standards he was thought praiseworthy—hence this comment. This is likeness causing error; corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note 17: The praise that Sheng, in the ground he trod, may be traced to the ancients—editions read Wei for Sheng. Zhang Wei's life does not fit; Dugu Sheng's death at Jiangdu does. Corrected from Wei to Sheng.

sentences.zh: [一八]陰世師遭天所廢舍命無改 諸本「世師」作「壽」．隋書卷三九史臣論作「世師」．按此指世師守長安拒李淵事，與陰壽無關，今據改．

translations.literal: [18] Yin Shishi was abandoned by heaven yet would not change his life. Various editions read "Shou" for "Shishi." Sui shu 39 historians' comment reads "Shishi." This refers to Shishi's defense of Chang'an against Li Yuan, unrelated to Yin Shou; amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note 18: The line that Yin Shishi, abandoned by heaven, would not change his life—some texts read Shou for Shishi. Sui shu 39's historians' comment has Shishi, referring to the defense of Chang'an, not Yin Shou—amended.
